revision_history: v1 (2026-09-19): initial draft after Phase 1 brief approval. Source channel: operator request after an evidence review found a foreign-instigation claim about southern Thailand unsupported; this issue is the documented half of the narrative-manipulation question. Frame: influence is a product sold by private firms to whoever pays; the receipts (Meta 2019/2022/2024, Forbidden Stories 2023, NYT 2024) name firms, a ministry and, once, Malaysia's police. Anchor: anger-at-process (a 2022 platform finding with no published police outcome; a 2025 statute that does not name the behaviour).
_provenance.discipline: Every operation is described by what the platform or consortium documented; the firm is named, the buyer only where a primary or authoritative report names one, and every named party's denial sits on the same card. The Israeli state appears once, as Stoic's reported and denied client. No card connects any of this to the southern Thailand conflict. The Archimedes-Malaysia audience line is AP's, attributed as such, because the lab's own write-up names no Malaysian page. No AI-provider name and no 'AI' appears on any card: the corroborating report by a second company stays in the brief; machine-generated text is not mentioned. Political HIGH, 3R LOW; Stage 5 not triggered at this stage.

headline: Fake pages are sold to whoever pays. The receipts name Israeli firms, a ministry and Malaysian police.
context: Since 2019 Meta has removed networks of fake local pages run by three Israeli firms, and one it linked to the Royal Malaysia Police. A journalism consortium filmed a fourth seller claiming 33 election campaigns. Malaysia's Online Safety Act 2025 does not name the behaviour.

cards.big: Meta removed 596 fake accounts and 180 Pages in August 2022 pushing pro-government memes and 'promoting police'. Its finding: 'links to the Royal Malaysia Police'.
cards.sub: Police denied it on 6 August 2022 and said they were gathering information. Nothing has been published since.

cards.big: Archimedes Group of Tel Aviv ran fake local news pages until Facebook removed 265 assets in May 2019: US$812,000 in ads, 2.8 million followers.
cards.sub: AP reported, citing the Atlantic Council's lab, that the largest audience was in Malaysia, a year after GE14. The lab's write-up names no Malaysian page.

cards.big: Tal Hanan was filmed claiming '33 presidential-level campaigns, 27 of which were successful', with software running 30,000 fake profiles, for sale to agencies and campaigns.
cards.sub: The 30-outlet consortium could not verify the count. Hanan denies wrongdoing. His firm sits on an Israeli defence-export register.

cards.big: Meta banned Stoic of Tel Aviv in May 2024 over 510 fake accounts posing as Jewish students and African Americans; the NYT reported an Israeli ministry paid about US$2m.
cards.sub: The ministry denies it. Malaysia's Online Safety Act 2025 has no clause on fake-account networks or foreign interference.

cards.big: AP reported an Israeli fake-news network's biggest audience was Malaysian. The troll farm Meta found here was traced to Malaysian police. The threat is a product, not a country.
It is like a print shop that stamps 'local' on every leaflet, hides its provenance, and sells to anyone, including, in one 2022 ledger, a police force.
cards.sub: Cambridge Analytica's website claimed a 2013 Kedah campaign for BN. BN, the PMO and Mukhriz denied paying; its Malaysia head said he advised Mukhriz personally.

cards.big: Singapore used its foreign-interference law in July 2024. Malaysia's police have owed an answer since August 2022. The product is for sale. Nobody here keeps the receipts.

confidence: High on every platform figure (Meta's own reports opened), on the Team Jorge quotes (Guardian text opened) and on the Act 866 absence (statute text opened and searched). Medium on the Malaysia-audience line: AP's sentence, attributed to the Atlantic Council lab, is not in the lab's own published analysis; the card says so. Medium on the Kedah dispute: three parties' statements, all secondary reporting of 2018. The 'ministry paid US$2m' figure is the NYT's, carried via Times of Israel with the denial.
needs_verification: AP's 'largest audience in Malaysia' sentence: DFRLab's own report (dfrlab.org mirror, opened) does not mention Malaysia. Stage 3 should decide whether AP's attribution stands; if not, the reframe's first sentence and fact 1's sub are dropped.
'Since August 2022' with no published outcome: searched PDRM statements and reporting 2022-2026; nothing found. Stage 3 should check Hansard and PDRM for any later statement.
'His firm sits on an Israeli defence-export register': Guardian wording is 'registered on a website run by the Israeli Ministry of Defense to promote defence exports'; card compresses.

Stoic accounts 'posing as Jewish students and African Americans': Meta's wording is 'posed as locals in the countries they targeted, including as Jewish students, African Americans and concerned citizens'.
'Three Israeli firms' in context: Archimedes (2019), Mind Force (2022), Stoic (2024), all in Meta reports; Team Jorge/Demoman is the 'fourth seller', exposed by journalists not Meta.
Singapore first FICA use: MHA press release URL returned 404; figure carried by Malay Mail and two law-firm bulletins.

Cambridge Analytica website wording for Kedah: Malaysian Insight paraphrase ('lists its work for Kedah BN'); Malay Mail quotes 'targeted messaging campaign highlighting school improvements since 2008'.

'Malaysia's police have owed an answer': the police said on 6 Aug 2022 they were 'gathering further information'; the card treats that as an undertaking to report. Stage 2 may read it as editorialising; the view card is the intended place for it.
source_notes: Archimedes ad spend: Meta US$812,000 (used) vs AP 'some $800,000' vs Wikipedia US$1.1m. Malaysia troll-farm count: Meta's itemised 596/180/11/72 used; outlets' 'close to 1,000' sums all asset types. Stoic client: NYT names the ministry; Meta names only the firm; the denial is on the card. Team Jorge's 33 is Hanan's own claim, attributed. A second company's May 2024 corroboration of the Stoic takedown is in the brief and deliberately off the cards under the content rules.
